verses.text: I wish my head were full of water and my eyes were springs of tears. Then I could cry day and night for the people of mine who’ve been killed.
I wish I had a shelter for travelers out in the wilderness. I’d leave my people and get away from them. They’re all adulterers, a whole crowd of traitors.

“They pull their tongues back like bows, ready to shoot lies. They’ve gained power in the land, but truth had nothing to do with it. They go from one evil to the next, and they don’t know me,” says the LORD.
“Watch out for your neighbors, every one of you, and don’t trust even a brother. Every brother will sneak in and take your place, and every neighbor goes around tearing people down.
Friends fool each other and refuse to tell the truth. They’ve trained their tongues to lie. They wear themselves out doing wrong.
You live right in the middle of all this lying. They cling to it and refuse to know me,” says the LORD.
So the LORD of Armies says, “Watch, I’m going to melt them down and test them. How else should I deal with my people?
Their tongues are deadly arrows. They shoot lies. A person talks peace to their neighbor’s face, while deep down they’re waiting to ambush them.
Shouldn’t I punish them for doing this?” says the LORD. “Shouldn’t I take vengeance on a nation that acts like this?

I’ll cry and wail for the mountains and mourn for the grazing land out in the wilderness. It’s all burned up. Nobody passes through, and you can’t hear the livestock anymore. The birds and the animals ran off. They’re gone.
“I’ll turn Jerusalem into piles of rubble where jackals live. I’ll leave Judah’s towns empty, with nobody living in them.”
Who’s wise enough to make sense of this? Who’s heard it from the LORD’s own mouth and can explain it? Why has the land been ruined and scorched like a desert nobody crosses?
The LORD says, “They threw away the law I laid out for them. They didn’t listen to me or live the way I told them to.
They followed their own stubborn hearts and went after the Baals, just like their ancestors taught them.”
So the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says, “Watch what I give these people to eat: bitter wormwood. And I’ll give them poisoned water to drink.
I’ll scatter them among nations they’ve never known, nations their ancestors never knew either. I’ll send the sword after them until I’ve finished them off.”
The LORD of Armies says, “Think about what’s happening. Call the women who mourn. Send for the ones who know how to do it, and have them come.
Tell them to hurry up and wail for us until tears run from our eyes and water pours from our eyelids.
There’s wailing coming out of Zion: ‘We’re ruined! We’re so ashamed! We’ve had to leave our land because they’ve torn down our homes.’”
Women, listen to what the LORD says. Take in the words from his mouth. Teach your daughters how to wail. Each of you, teach your neighbor a song of grief.
Death has climbed in through our windows. It’s made its way into our palaces. It’s cutting down the children outside and the young men in the streets.
Say this: “The LORD says, ‘Bodies will drop like dung across the open fields, like handfuls of grain left behind a harvester. Nobody will pick them up.’”
The LORD says, “If you’re wise, don’t brag about how wise you are. If you’re strong, don’t brag about your strength. If you’re rich, don’t brag about your money.

If you’re going to boast, boast about this: that you understand and know me, that I’m the LORD who shows faithful love, brings justice, and does what’s right on earth. That’s what I delight in,” says the LORD.
“Look, the days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I’ll punish everyone whose circumcision is only skin deep:

Egypt, Judah, Edom, the people of Ammon, Moab, and everyone in the wilderness who cuts off the corners of their hair. All those nations are uncircumcised, and the whole family of Israel is uncircumcised at heart.”
